newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel fire report in few weeks.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel fire report in few weeks.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc, the Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator, said on Wednesday that it would release the results of the inquiry into the tunnel fire last November in the coming weeks.

A spokeswoman for Eurotunnel said "We will be publishing the results of the inquiry in the next few weeks and hold a briefing into the results. But we will not comment on any individual aspects ahead of this -- everything has to be in context."
Last November's fire damaged a large section of one of the tunnels and severely hit passenger and freight services.
Eurotunnel refused to be drawn on a report in the Financial Times newspaper on Wednesday, which said it had ruled out the possible redesign of its open-sided freight wagons.
The Kent Fire Brigade said in the aftermath of the blaze that the wagon design had helped intensify the fire, with the open-sided wagons acting like a "blow-torch".
The FT said the design had been given a "clean bill of health", however, and that Eurotunnel would only recommend changes to safety systems and equipment improvements.

Eurotunnel's spokesman refused to elaborate and would only say that the report "may make some suggestions aimed at procedures." Eurotunnel's own report will be followed by one from the Anglo-French Channel Tunnel Safety Authority which is not expected to insist on major redesign of the wagons, said the FT.
